1.explanation:
1. lighthouse-core/audits/manifest-short-name-length.js is where the audit reads the artifact’s short_name and checks its length against the maximum. It currently assumes short_name is always present (or falls back to an empty string), so when short_name is missing the audit fails. The fix should be here: skip the length check or fall back to name when short_name is undefined.  
2. lighthouse-core/lib/manifest-parser.js is responsible for parsing the raw manifest JSON into the artifact passed to the audit. It normalizes undefined properties (including short_name) to empty strings, which feeds the length-check audit with a 0-length string instead of allowing the audit to detect the field’s absence. Adjusting the parser to preserve the distinction between a missing short_name and an empty string (or to forward the name field) is required to avoid the false positive.
1.bug_scenario: When a web app manifest omits the “short_name” field—even if it has a valid “name”—the manifest-short-name-length audit treats the missing short_name as an empty string, computes its length as 0, and throws a “Found: 0 chars” failure (a false positive) reporting that it’s below the suggested maximum of 12 characters.

2.explanation:
• lighthouse-core/audits/manifest-short-name-length.js: This is the audit that measures the length of the manifest’s short_name and currently doesn’t guard against the field being missing. It treats an empty string as a failure rather than skipping the check when short_name is undefined.
• lighthouse-core/lib/manifest-parser.js: The manifest-parser normalizes missing manifest properties but defaults short_name to an empty string. That forces the length audit to see “” instead of undefined. To fix the bug, the parser should leave short_name undefined when absent (or the audit should explicitly ignore empty/missing short_name).
2.bug_scenario: When a web app manifest omits the “short_name” field (even if it does define a valid “name”), the manifest-short-name-length audit treats the missing field as an empty string and computes its length as 0. The audit then fails with “Found: 0 chars” and reports a false positive against the 12-character maximum.
